questions.question: What does `const { role: jobTitle } = user` do?
options: Creates a variable named role with the value of user.jobTitle
Destructures user.role into a new variable named jobTitle
Throws a SyntaxError — renaming during destructuring isn't allowed
Creates two separate variables, role and jobTitle, both equal to user.role
questions.explanation: The `oldName: newName` syntax in object destructuring pulls out a property under a different local variable name.

questions.question: After `const overridden = { ...base, fontSize: 16 }`, what happens to nested objects inside `base` if `overridden` mutates one of them?
options: Nothing changes in base — spread always creates a full deep copy
base is also affected, because spread only performs a shallow copy; nested objects are still shared by reference
Spread cannot be used with objects containing nested objects
questions.explanation: Spread copies top-level properties only; any nested object or array value is still the same reference in both the original and the copy.

questions.question: Which array method is the most general, in the sense that `map` and `filter` could both be implemented using it?
questions.explanation: reduce folds an array down to any accumulated value, including a transformed array (map's job) or a filtered array (filter's job).

questions.question: In `function sum(...numbers) { ... }`, what does the `...` before `numbers` do?
options: Spreads an existing array into individual arguments
Collects all remaining arguments passed to the function into a single array called numbers (a rest parameter)
It's a syntax error outside of array literals
questions.explanation: Inside a function parameter list, `...name` is a rest parameter, gathering any number of trailing arguments into one array.
